Q: Technical Issue: Pie Chart Slice "Distance from Center" and "Color" not updating via Apps Script A:

Apparently, the Spreadsheet Service (Class SpreadsheetApp) and the Advanced Sheets Service are not able to set the slice options for an embedded chart in Google Sheets:

  • When trying to get the slices option of a pie chart embedded in a spreadsheet, null is returned.

  • PieChartSpec doesn't include the slices property.

If you really need to create a pie chart with custom slice options, you can use Google Charts with HTML/CSS/JavaScript. For details, see https://developers.google.com/chart, more specifically, see https://developers.google.com/chart/interactive/docs/gallery/piechart

Note: The Google Apps Script HTML Service can be used to display a Google Chart.

Q: Memory settings for running Maven Builds within Docker A:

I have a few things that are red herrings.

a) you find the metaspace usage "absurd", but you seem to have no qualms about the tests consuming up gigabytes of memory to cause the JVM to be put in that state. I have no idea why you would think Maven is in any way involved in that process. High non-heap usage tends to follow from high heap usage. And it might just be... normal. But you provide no details about your application, what tech stack is being used and what your tests are doing so nobody but you really can know that. You are talking about the surefire plugin rather than the failsafe plugin though, so these are unit tests we are talking about? If so, that makes it extra questionable to me. Integration tests tend to do more memory hungry things like booting up testcontainers and starting an entire application context/server. I can't imagine what your unit tests are doing to eat that much memory.

b) you fork a JVM (your decision or your team's decision by the way and thus your responsibility), a very memory intensive process, and then seem to be shocked by the fact that this has drastic consequences especially for running in a container. Based on the fact that you state "The setting --XX:MaxRAMPercentage=90 affects both the original JVM and the forked JVM utilized by Surefire", that would lead me to believe you are not setting an argLine to then configure this forked JVM. Correct? If so... it isn't exactly a mystery you are having so much trouble containing your forked beast. But it is all documented, right here: https://maven.apache.org/surefire/maven-surefire-plugin/examples/fork-options-and-parallel-execution.html

No it's not clearly Maven. But you provide no details at all, so I don't think in this state anyone could really tell you where to look or what to read.

Q: React native expo Flatlist with items containing an input field A:

Creating input for each list items is anti-pattern and performance bottleneck and raise conflict swith behavior of FlatList virtualization and Keyboard input focus.

What client need is ability to add item quantity for each product. You can achieve this without compromise performance and fight with React Native way of working.

For each Product list add button to edit quantity, when pressed it open BottomSheet with input to type quantity and update accordingly.

By this approach, user will be able to change quantity for any product and you will use only single Input which is recommended.

Q: Express static files (CSS/JS/images) return 404 on Railway but work locally A:

If I were you, I will always validate the Deployed fileSystem. Railways allow you to open Shell into the running Container.

ls -la // this shows all files and folder in the current directory
ls -la public //shows everything inside the public folder, including hidden files.

when you see something goes weird run that command immediately.
